items.title: Latin America Currencies Sink on Rate Worries; Brazil Intervenes
points: (Bloomberg) -- A sell-off in Latin American currencies deepened Thursday, sending the Mexican peso to its lowest since June 2025 and forcing Brazil’s central bank to step in to prop up the real, amid the mounting prospect of more rate hikes in the US.
The Colombian peso led losses across emerging markets, tumbling as much as 3.4% against the greenback.

And in Brazil, the real dropped nearly 0.7% as investors shrugged off the first dollar spot auction since late 2024, which came after President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva said he was in no rush to announce a new finance minister.
The moves weighed on MSCI’s EM currency index, which fell 0.2% and is on track for a fourth week of declines — the longest such streak since March.

The pressure on Latin America is partly driven by domestic issues, such as fiscal worries in Brazil, a dovish central bank in Mexico, recessionary headwinds in Chile and the potential dilution of the fiscal reform in Colombia, said Benito Berber, chief…

items.title: Japanese investors sought $9.4 billion of shares in Anthropic IPO, sources say
points: TOKYO, - Japanese investors sought to buy more than 1.5 trillion yen worth of Anthropic shares at its public listing this week, two people familiar with the offer said.
Japanese investors ultimately secured $2.98 billion worth of the shares, a filing showed on Thursday.
Anthropic raised $81 billion in total worldwide in what became the world's largest initial public offering on record, eclipsing SpaceX, which raised $75 billion at its listing in June.
Anthropic ultimately priced its offering at $83 per share, above its initial range of $70 to $78.

Some Japanese investors saw Anthropic as the frontrunner among AI firms and so justified large orders, said the people, who spoke on the condition of anonymity because they were not authorised to discuss the ​IPO publicly.

Other investors sought smaller allocations or sat out the offering altogether, seeing greater prospective returns in semiconductor stocks that have fallen sharply, such as Nvidia and Kioxia, or in waiting for OpenAI’s listing due next year, one of the…

items.title: Trinamool party symbol row: Abhishek Banerjee says twin flower symbol will return in seven days
points: Mamata All India Trinamool Congress MP Abhishek Banerjee has claimed that the faction of the party led by Ritabrata Banerjee filed affidavits with the help of the West Bengal Police.

File. | Photo Credit: ANI The two rival factions of the Trinamool Congress have become embroiled in a war of words over the party’s twin-flower symbol that has been frozen by the Election Commission of India (ECI).
Diamond Harbour MP Abhishek Banerjee and Mamata All India Trinamool Congress on November 18 said that the original electoral symbol of the party will ultimately remain with Mamata Banerjee.
The Diamond Harbour MP had claimed that the alleged attack on his residence on November 7 was intended to interfere with the filing of affidavits, staking a claim over the affidavits.

Leader of the Opposition in the West Bengal Assembly Ritabrata Banerjee said that the symbol does not belong to either faction and Mr. Banerjee will not be able to stake claim over the symbol in seven births.

GTA 6, however, lets you put a little more thought behind the kind of criminal you want to become.

While infinite inventory is gone, the GTA 6 weapon wheel is sticking around with some visual tweaks.
So, learn everything about the GTA 6 weapon wheel and inventory system.
The GTA 6 weapon wheel keeps the familiar radial format, but with a more minimalist and colorful design instead of its predecessor’s circular wheel.

items.title: Uttarakhand Bank Manager, 2 Agents Arrested In Rs 9 Lakh Bribery Case
points: A Bank of Baroda branch manager and two intermediaries here have been arrested for demanding a cut for sanctioning a loan to an applicant, the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) said on Thursday.

The CBI registered an instant case on November 18 against the manager of the bank's Indira Nagar branch in Dehradun and two private persons working as Direct Selling Agents (DSA), based on a complaint.
The complainant alleged that they demanded a bribe of 5 per cent of the loan amount in exchange for facilitating the sanction and disbursement of the Rs 1.8 crore loan.

The CBI statement mentioned that for sanctioning and disbursal of the said loan, the accused persons had earlier obtained a partial bribe amount of Rs 2.5 lakh in cash from the complainant and insisted upon him to make the remaining payment of Rs 6.5 lakh.

items.title: Advocates, traders protest in Vaniyambadi for additional district court
points: Litigants, advocate, and court staff find the commute from one court to another challenging. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement Advocates, traders and residents staged a protest near a bus terminus in Vaniyambadi town on Thursday, demanding an additional…
The protest was held in the wake of the onset of the Northeast monsoon, when it could be risky to conduct court proceedings at the dilapidated Judicial Magistrate court.
Each court, on an average, is located at least 1.5 km away from the other court.
The Judicial Magistrate Court, the oldest among three courts, was located in the Government Estate since the 1920s.
The District Munsif court, formed in 1995, was functioning from a rented room in the Government Commercial Tax building.
Every day, on an average, more than 150 litigants, mostly from Vaniyambadi taluk that comprises 45 villages, visit these courts.
Around 75 advocates are working as regular practitioners.
On an average, over 100 cases come up at each court every day.

items.title: CBI secures deportation of murder accused wanted by Kerala Police from UAE
points: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), in coordination with the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA), the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) and the Kerala Police, has secured the deportation of Raghesh Unnikochan, against whom a Red Notice had been issued,…
He was wanted in connection with a murder case registered by the Kerala Police.
The incident occurred on October 1, 2008, at Thirumangalam, Thrissur.
At the request of the Kerala Police, NCB-New Delhi (CBI) had secured the publication of a Red Notice against the accused through Interpol channels.
After the accused was geo-located and arrested by the UAE authorities, the latter approved his deportation to India following due legal process, a statement issued by the investigation agency said.
The accused was handed over to an escort team of the Kerala Police in the UAE.

The CBI, as the National Central Bureau for Interpol in India, coordinates with law enforcement agencies across the country through BHARATPOL, an online portal developed by the CBI to facilitate international police cooperation.

items.title: Azam Khan's 'Biryani' Jibe At Asaduddin Owaisi Amid Tussle For UP Muslim Votes

He has even forged an alliance with Dalit leader Chandrasekhar Azad's Azad Samaj Party, hoping to carve a niche within the state's Dalit-Muslim votebank.
Uttar Pradesh has nearly 20 per cent Muslims, the Dalit population is over 20 per cent.
In 2022 also, Owaisi's AIMIM had contested in Uttar Pradesh, putting up candidates in nearly 100 seats.
This time, Owaisi has launched multiple attacks against the Samajwadi Party and its ally Congress, invoking the 1987 Hashimpura and Maliana massacres and the 2013 Muzaffarnagar riots.

items.title: Kerala High Court disposes of PILs against reconstitution of Waqf Board
points: A Division Bench of the Kerala High Court on Thursday disposed of all public interest litigations (PILs) related to the reconstitution of the Kerala State Waqf Board.
The Bench observed that the reconstitution of the board had given rise to a fresh cause of action, following which the aggrieved parties had filed writ petitions.
It said the petitions were required to be heard by a Single Judge in accordance with the roster.
The High Court had in October refused to stay the reconstitution of the board.
The court was considering appeals filed by former board chairperson K.S.
Usman Haji against a Single Bench order refusing to stay the reconstitution.
The court had then held that a stay could not be granted as the new board had taken charge.
The State had reconstituted the board on October 16 and nominated nine new members.

items.title: Resignation not admission of wrongdoing, I am innocent: Justice Varma tells Lok Sabha secretariat
points: New Delhi, Justice Yashwant Varma has asserted that he is innocent of the allegations relating to the discovery of burnt currency notes at his official residence and that his resignation as a high court judge should not be construed as an acknowledgement…

Citing Article 217 of the Constitution and a 1978 Constitution Bench judgment of the Supreme Court in 'Union of India vs Gopal Chandra Mishra', he argued that a high court judge's resignation takes effect by its own force and does not require acceptance by…

items.title: Cheran, the poet who chronicled Eelam’s war and memory, passes away at 68
points: Eelam Tamil poet, essayist, and academic Rudhramoorthy Cheran passed away in Canada on Wednesday.
At the time of his passing, he was a professor in the Department of Sociology and Criminology at the University of Windsor.
Hailing from Alaveddy in Jaffna, Cheran was a multifaceted artist — a poet, short story writer, essayist, and painter.
After beginning his literary career in the late 1970s, he emerged as a central figure in the Eelam Tamil literary movement during the 1980s.
Although he started writing in the 1970s, his debut poetry collection, Irandavathu Sooriya Uthayam (The Second Sunrise), was published in 1983.

Reflecting on Cheran’s literary significance, poet and Kalachuvadu executive editor Sukumaran notes: “Having begun writing in the 70s, Cheran bore witness to the Eelam war as it intensified in the 80s.

Cheran documented four to five decades of Eelam Tamil life and brought their reality to the world stage.” Cheran’s poetry has been compiled into several acclaimed collections, including Nee Ippothu Irangum Aaru, Kaadaatru, Meendum Kadalukku,…

items.title: AAP Government Faces Fire After Court Halts Punjab Civil Services Recruitment
points: The Punjab and Haryana High Court's decision to halt the entire Punjab Civil Services (PCS) recruitment process has triggered a fresh political confrontation in the state, with the main Opposition party Congress and the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) accusing…

Punjab Congress president Pargat Singh termed the court's decision "a major victory for the state's youth", saying it vindicated the concerns repeatedly raised by aspirants over alleged irregularities in the recruitment process.
He questioned why the government and the Punjab Public Service Commission (PPSC) had failed to address candidates' complaints despite repeated representations.

Pointing out that 331 posts were advertised and 751 candidates were shortlisted for the next stage after the mains examination results were declared, Pargat Singh said the Congress would continue its fight for a fair recruitment process.

"Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann must answer to the youth of Punjab as to why his government failed to take timely action on the serious questions raised over the recruitment process," Pargat Singh said.

items.title: Evicted Families Relocate To New Area In Assam, Face Bulldozer Action Again
points: A fresh eviction drive was carried out at Bali Chapori in Boginodi in Assam's Lakhimpur district on Thursday, removing families who had relocated to the area after being evicted from Professional Grazing Reserve (PGR) land earlier this week.
The operation began in the morning, with the district administration deploying police personnel and officials at the site.
Bulldozers were used to clear the area as security forces remained deployed to maintain law and order.
At least 132 families were evicted from PGR land in Boginodi during an earlier drive earlier this week.
With their previous homes cleared, some of them had taken shelter at Bali Chapori.
The administration subsequently launched another eviction drive at the site, clearing the makeshift shelters where the displaced families had been staying.
The drive left the families facing displacement once again, within days of their removal from the PGR land.
With the latest eviction, the affected families have been forced to leave the places where they had sought refuge following the earlier operation.

items.title: Resignation Not Admission Of Guilt: Justice Yashwant Varma Tells Lok Sabha Secretariat
points: Justice Yashwant Varma has contended that proceedings for his removal as a high court judge became infructuous following his resignation and cannot be continued, saying any attempt to remove him from office would be without constitutional foundation.
In a letter dated September 10 to Lok Sabha Secretary General Utpal Kumar Singh, he responded to the report of the inquiry committee constituted by Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla.
Varma wrote that the proceedings directed towards his removal did not survive his resignation.

He reiterated that he was innocent of the allegations against him, including the suggestion that he possessed ill-gotten funds, and asserted that his resignation should not be construed as an acknowledgement or admission of any allegation or finding.
The three-member inquiry committee, in its report tabled in Parliament on August 12, had found all three charges against Justice Varma proved.

items.title: APSRTC outsourced staff allege exploitation, seek fair deal
points: A delegation led by AITUC State general secretary S.
Venkata Subbaiah, APSRTC Outsourced Employees’ Union State president Dasari Kiran Kumar and State general secretary T.
Ganga Anjaneyulu met APSRTC Joint Managing Director Sivaprasad in Vijayawada on Thursday and submitted a memorandum, highlighting the problems being faced by the outsourced employees.

The union leaders said more than 8,500 outsourced workers have been serving across 26 districts, 129 depots, four zonal workshops, bus stations, hospitals, stores and other APSRTC establishments for several years.
They alleged that workers were facing delayed salary payments, wage discrepancies, irregularities in Provident Fund (PF) and Employees’ State Insurance (ESI) deposits and lack of job security.
Mr. Kiran Kumar demanded the abolition of the third-party contracting system and the inclusion of all outsourcing employees under Andhra Pradesh Corporation for Outsourced Services (APCOS).
He sought direct salary transfers into workers’ bank accounts by APSRTC before the 10th of every month, equal wages on par with outsourced employees in other government departments and job security.

items.title: Offshore Chinese Yuan Drops to Weakest Level in Over a Month
points: (Bloomberg) -- The offshore Chinese yuan declined to the weakest level in more than a month while the dollar rallied as risk appetite shrank.
The yuan fell as much as 0.5% to touch 6.6999 against the US dollar on Thursday, the lowest since mid-October.
The Chinese currency sold off along with many other emerging market currencies, including the Colombian peso, the South African rand and the Hungarian forint.
A gauge of EM currencies is down 0.1%, while the Bloomberg Dollar Spot Index is up 0.2%.
“The yuan has been grinding higher for quite some time, and the market appears to have been caught off-guard today,” said Alex Cohen, a strategist at the Bank of America.

“The broader dollar rally is making emerging markets increasingly less attractive.” Both the offshore yuan and its onshore counterpart, which trades inside mainland China and is state managed, have advanced about 4% against the dollar this year.

items.title: Eurozone Current Account Surplus Narrows
points: The eurozone current account surplus narrowed to €27.5 billion in September 2026, down from €32.6 billion a year earlier, reflecting a sharp decline in the goods surplus to €16.2 billion from €31.8 billion.
In contrast, the services surplus widened to €23.7 billion from €16.3 billion, while the primary income surplus increased to €3.5 billion from almost zero.
Meanwhile, the secondary income deficit remained broadly stable at €15.9 billion, compared with €15.5 billion in September 2025.
For the first nine months of 2026, the cumulative current account surplus declined to €160.0 billion, from €180.8 billion in the same period of 2025.

items.title: PUC Certificate Rules – BSVI Cars Get More Time
points: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) has amended Rule 115 of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989, to revise the validity periods of Pollution Under Control (PUC) certificates.
The Central Motor Vehicles (Sixteenth Amendment) Rules, 2026, were notified on 13 November 2026 through G.S.R.
Under the amended rules, PUC certificate validity will depend on the vehicle’s emission standard, category and age.
Vehicles complying with BS-IV emission standards will have a validity period of six months.
For BS-VI non-transport vehicles, the revised schedule introduces three age-based validity periods.
Vehicles up to six years old, calculated from their first registration date, will receive PUC certificates valid for three years.
Those exceeding ten years will need a fresh certificate every six months.
Those aged more than six years but not exceeding ten years will require annual renewal.

points: Fintech majors came under severe selling pressure on Thursday, with Pine Labs, Paytm and One MobiKwik Systems falling as much as 9% after reports emerged of a possible delay in implementing the proposed Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) framework for select…

The government is considering delaying the rollout of a fee on large payments made through its popular Unified Payments Interface platform by a few months, Reuters reported, citing sources familiar with the matter.
The proposed charge will apply to person-to-merchant (P2M) UPI payments above ₹2,000.
It will be borne by merchants, not consumers, and capped at ₹300 for transactions of ₹75,000 or more.

The fee, which was scheduled to come into effect from October 15, would have coincided with India's annual festive season, which runs from October through December and typically sees a surge in consumer spending.

A delay in the MDR rollout could push back the potential revenue opportunity for fintech companies such as Paytm and Pine Labs, which have been anticipating the move to monetise large-value merchant transactions.

items.title: Wreck Of Australia’s First Home-Built Warship Found 128 Years After It Sank
points: The wreck of HMCS Spitfire, a small gunboat that holds the distinction of being the earliest warship built in Australia to serve Australians, has been found off the coast of Far North Queensland, exactly 128 years after it sank.
Royal Australian Navy teams located the site on August 21, 2026, after a month-long search.
Experts from Queensland’s state environment department and the Australian National Maritime Museum then verified that the remains belonged to the lost gunboat.
HMCS Spitfire was launched in 1855 from a shipyard on Darling Harbour in Sydney.
The 16-metre gunboat was built to serve an Australian colonial government and patrolled the coastal waters of New South Wales.
The former warship sank in 1898 while on a voyage off Far North Queensland after a working life of more than 40 years.
A senior heritage officer from the Queensland environment department said it was ‘remarkable luck’ that HMCS Spitfire was found on the 128th anniversary of its sinking.

items.title: India Signs ₹1,976 Crore Deal With Israel To Upgrade Indian Navy’s Barak Missile Systems
points: Barak missile systems fitted on Indian warships are set for an upgrade after India signed a deal of Rs 1,976.40 crore, about $211 million, with Israel Aerospace Industries (IAI).
The contract was inked by India’s Ministry of Defence in New Delhi on November 18, 2026, with Defence Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh present for the signing.
The deal, including obsolescence management for the missile system, followed India’s Other Capital Procurement Procedure.
Barak-1 is a point defence missile system which is fitted onboard ships to intercept aircraft, drones and anti-ship missiles, including sea-skimmers.
The Indian Navy procured the Barak-1 in 2000 and has installed it on several of its frontline warships to date.
These warships include the aircraft carrier INS Vikramaditya along with Delhi-class destroyers and Shivalik-class and Brahmaputra-class frigates.
The upgrade had been cleared by India’s Defence Acquisition Council in August 2025 as part of proposals worth around Rs 67,000 crore for the armed forces.

items.title: Dhan launches SIF investing, offering long-short strategies at ₹10 lakh entry point
points: The announcement was made on November 19, 2026.
The platform currently lists over 30 SIF strategies across SEBI-permitted categories from multiple asset management companies.
SIFs were introduced by SEBI under the Mutual Fund framework in April 2025, granting fund managers broader flexibility beyond traditional long-only mandates.

Under an Equity Long-Short strategy, managers can hold long positions in stocks expected to appreciate while simultaneously taking short positions through derivatives in stocks anticipated to decline.
Dhan’s CEO and Founder Pravin Jadhav positioned the offering as a more accessible alternative to Portfolio Management Services, which typically require a minimum investment of ₹50 lakh.
A Split Orders feature allows investors to distribute the ₹10 lakh minimum across multiple eligible strategies from the same AMC.
The SIF launch follows Dhan’s earlier additions of Mutual Funds in December 2023 and, more recently, Stock Rental via SLBM, Gold Vault, and US Stocks and ETFs.
Dhan currently ranks among the top 10 stock trading platforms by active clients on NSE, with 11.46 lakh traders on its platform.

items.title: USS George Washington Leaves Middle East After 3 Months As US Carrier Count Drops To 2
points: Aircraft carrier USS George Washington has sailed out of the Middle East after a three-month stay, leaving only two U.S. carriers in the region.
The Japan-based carrier is now under the control of the U.S. Pacific Fleet and is performing regular operations across the Asia-Pacific, a fleet spokesperson said on November 18.
The Nimitz-class carrier has moved into the U.S. 7th Fleet region, though the spokesperson did not say which escort ships sailed along with it.
USS George Washington had reached the U.S. 5th Fleet area on August 19 along with the cruiser USS Robert Smalls and the destroyer USS Shoup.
Before heading to the Middle East, the carrier made port calls in Vietnam and Guam and patrolled the Philippine Sea after leaving Yokosuka in late May.
The aircraft carrier USS Theodore Roosevelt arrived in the Middle East on November 15, shortly before the George Washington departed.

items.title: Indian Navy Marks 50 Years Of Long-Range Maritime Reconnaissance
points: The Indian Navy completed 50 years of Long-Range Maritime Reconnaissance (LRMR) flying on November 18, 2026, a date which also marks the 50th anniversary of its squadron INAS 312.
INAS 312 was named Albatross and was commissioned in 1976 at INS Hansa in Goa, India, with a fleet of five Lockheed Super Constellation planes.
The Indian Air Force transferred these aircraft to the Navy for this role.
It was after the 1971 war that the Navy realised it required shore-based patrol aircraft for operating with its ships and helicopters, and took charge of long-range reconnaissance.
In 1977, the Ilyushin Il-38 was inducted, and it boosted the Navy’s reconnaissance as well as anti-submarine warfare (ASW) strength.
The Tupolev Tu-142M came to INAS 312 in 1988 and enabled the Navy to patrol farther across the Indian Ocean Region.
The latest addition was the Boeing P-8I, which came to INS Rajali in Arakkonam in 2013.

items.title: Ships Receiving Iranian Cargo At Sea Could Be Seized As US Tightens Iran Blockade
points: Ship-to-ship transfers involving cargo loaded in Iran could now get the receiving vessels stopped or seized at sea under a U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) update issued on November 18, 2026.
Under the new guidance, U.S. forces could board and capture ships involved in such ship-to-ship transfers or send them to the Iranian port where the cargo was first loaded.
The update was shared with shipowners and seafarers by the Joint Maritime Information Centre (JMIC) in its advisory note 017-26.
The blockade covers every Iranian port along with the entire Iranian coastline and its oil terminals, and it applies to ships of all flags.
The U.S. first imposed a naval blockade on Iran-related oil exports on April 13 and lifted it in June after reaching a draft understanding with Iran, according to reports.
Neutral ships can continue to transit the Strait of Hormuz to non-Iranian destinations, although they remain subject to search.

items.title: Royal Navy Tests New Rotating Decoy System To Protect Warships From Anti-Ship Missiles
points: Royal Navy warships are set to get a new rotating decoy launcher called Ancilia, which can turn to face incoming anti-ship missiles instead of firing from fixed tubes.
The navy’s electromagnetic warfare specialists have tested its controls in two days of trials and rated it a marked improvement over the current system.
Four Electromagnetic Warfare Directors carried out these trials at the facility of the manufacturer SEA in Barnstaple in the English county of Devon.
The launcher fires the existing 130mm decoy rounds, including chaff and flares along with smoke and radio frequency reflectors that lure an incoming missile away from the ship.
SEA won a £135 million contract in 2024 to deliver 38 launchers for 19 warships, with two launchers planned for each ship.
These ships include six Type 45 destroyers along with eight Type 26 and five Type 31 frigates.

items.title: World’s Busiest Cruise Port PortMiami Crosses 10 Million Passengers For The First Time
points: PortMiami in the U.S. state of Florida has crossed the 10 million mark in cruise passenger traffic for the first time in its history, setting a new global record.
As per the Miami-Dade County administration, the port saw 10,533,854 cruise passengers in its 2026 fiscal year as against 8,564,225 passengers in the previous year.
The figures show that around two million additional passengers passed through the port this year, taking the total up by 23%.
The fiscal year of the port began on October 1, 2025 and ended on September 30, 2026.

The trend has carried on into the first month of the new fiscal year where PortMiami recorded 832,142 cruise passengers across 106 cruise calls in October 2026, which is the best October the port has seen till now.
The passenger count for October has thus gone up by 19.04% while the number of cruise calls has risen by 13.98%.

items.title: South Korea Launches Advanced 3,600-Tonne Stealth Frigate Equipped With Indigenous Radar
points: South Korea has launched a new 3,600-tonne stealth frigate named Pyeongtaek that comes fitted with a homegrown phased array radar, as the country continues to strengthen its naval defence.
The warship was launched in a ceremony held on November 18, 2026, at the Hanwha Ocean shipyard in the southern city of Geoje.

The Pyeongtaek is the fifth vessel of the Ulsan-class Batch-III program, under which the Republic of Korea Navy aims to replace its ageing frigates and patrol combat corvettes, the Navy said in a joint statement with the country’s arms procurement agency.
Nearly 150 people were present at the event, among them Defense Minister Kang Shin-chul.
As per the Minister, the new frigate would be part of the 2nd Fleet and stand guard over the Yellow Sea, which he called a core bastion of the country’s defence.
The frigate is equipped with a locally developed Multifunctional Phased Array Radar.

items.title: Torm hits back at Hafnia over rejected merger bids
points: Danish product tanker giant Torm has hit back at Hafnia following its abandoned takeover pursuit, revealing that it rejected several merger proposals from its rival because they offered no meaningful premium and substantially undervalued the company.

The Jacob Meldgaard-led owner broke its silence after BW Group-backed Hafnia announced plans to exit its near-20% stake, bringing an end to its attempts to combine two of the world’s largest product tanker operators.
Torm chairman Simon Mackenzie Smith defended the decision, arguing that Hafnia had failed to recognise the company’s operating performance and future prospects.
“The proposals from Hafnia fundamentally failed to recognize that track record and the significant future value embedded in the One Torm platform,” he said.
The response comes after Hafnia chief executive Søren Steenberg Jensen announced that the company was walking away from its consolidation ambitions, having failed to secure Torm’s support.

items.title: Industries Minister: Bengaluru Designs Electric Scooters, Why Are The Factories In Tamil Nadu?
points: Bengaluru has become an important centre for electric two-wheeler engineering, but Karnataka is worried that too many of the resulting manufacturing jobs are going elsewhere.

State industries minister MB Patil has highlighted the gap between design offices in Bengaluru and factories across the border in Tamil Nadu, while proposing new industrial parks to make Karnataka a more attractive place to build vehicles.

Speaking to entrepreneurs and investors at the Bengaluru Tech Summit on November 18, Patil said that several electric two-wheeler companies operate design teams in the city while most of their production takes place outside the state.
Ather Energy has manufacturing operations in Hosur, Tamil Nadu, a short distance from Bengaluru.
Ola Electric also has a major manufacturing base in Tamil Nadu.
River Mobility, which makes the Indie electric scooter, is an important exception, with production in Hoskote near Bengaluru.
Patil said the government is exploring a startup and industrial park spread across roughly 1,000 acres near Bengaluru, along with another 100 to 200 acres near Hubballi-Dharwad.

items.title: Naini Lake’s duck population falls as rats prey on eggs in Uttarakhand: Official
points: The duck population at Naini Lake in Uttarakhand’s Nainital has fallen sharply over the past decade, with only a dozen birds remaining as rats prey on their eggs and disrupt their breeding cycle, raising concerns over the lake’s biodiversity, officials and…
The municipal authorities are exploring measures to protect the ducks and control the growing rat population around Naini Lake, one of Nainital’s major tourist attractions.
Nainital municipality is responsible for the maintenance of Naini Lake.
Nainital municipality chairperson Saraswati Khetwal said, “The rat population around Naini Lake had increased considerably over the years and the number of ducks has come down to around 14.
The rodents not only burrow into the ground in areas surrounding the lake but also destroy duck eggs, contributing to concerns over the declining bird population.
The ducks have long been part of Naini Lake’s natural landscape, and their dwindling numbers have drawn attention to the challenges facing the local ecosystem.
“Around a decade ago, more than 100 ducks could be seen in the lake.

items.title: Houston Ship Pilot Becomes First In US History To Face Seaman’s Manslaughter Charge

Officials have said this is the first time in U.S. history that a ship pilot is facing such a charge.
As per the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of Texas, 39-year-old Darris Ornel Jefferson has been indicted in a case announced on November 18, 2026.
He is due to make his first appearance in court before a magistrate judge on November 24.

items.title: Hanwha Philly Shipyard Begins Building First American-Built MR Tanker In 10 Years
points: Hanwha Philly Shipyard in the United States has begun construction on the first of four medium-range (MR) tankers for Hanwha Shipping, with steel cutting for the vessel taking place on November 17, 2026.
The oil and chemical tankers will be built under the Jones Act for the American coastal trade and are scheduled for delivery in 2029 and 2030.
As per the shipyard, the tankers will feature an energy-efficient design and will meet the Type 2 and Type 3 rules of the International Maritime Organization (IMO) for the carriage of chemicals.
Hanwha Shipping was formed in April 2024 and is owned by the South Korean shipbuilder Hanwha Ocean.
The order comes shortly after Hanwha Philly Shipyard was selected for the Landing Ship Medium (LSM) program, which the company has called its first shipbuilding opportunity from the U.S. Navy.
In October 2026, the yard christened the containership Makua, which it is building for the American shipping company Matson.

The contract covers installing riser clamps and bow strings for ONGC’s offshore pipeline replacement programme.
According to the company’s stock exchange filing, Larsen & Toubro’s Energy Hydrocarbon division awarded the work to POSH.
The contract is valued at approximately $10.77m, excluding applicable taxes, with execution scheduled for completion by May 2027.
PRP-X forms part of ONGC’s programme to replace ageing offshore pipeline infrastructure off India’s west coast.
Larsen & Toubro secured the main engineering, procurement, construction, installation, and commissioning (EPCIC) package in August.
Seamec had previously disclosed a separate letter of award from Larsen & Toubro to its consortium with POSH in early November, identifying a $26.14m share of the PRP-X installation work.

items.title: Superyacht Bayesian Had Unrecognised Vulnerability To High Winds Before Sinking That Killed 7
points: Superyacht Bayesian had a vulnerability to high winds that its crew did not know about before it was knocked onto its side and sank off Sicily in Italy.
Britain’s Marine Accident Investigation Branch made this finding in a final report on the sinking, publicised on November 19, 2026.
The 56-metre sailing yacht was at anchor about half a nautical mile south-east of the port of Porticello when a violent downburst of hurricane-force winds struck it at 4.06 am on August 19, 2024.
Seven people lost their lives in the sinking, including British tech entrepreneur Mike Lynch and his daughter Hannah, who was 18.
Chief Inspector of Marine Accidents said that calm weather gave way to winds of 68 knots or more over a period of only 14 minutes.
The 15 survivors in the water were helped into this liferaft and were later picked up by a nearby vessel before being taken ashore.

items.title: Stalin calls Tamil Nadu ‘Vice City’ under CM Vijay, then comes cops' GTA-themed post
points: DMK chief M K Stalin on Thursday accused the Vijay-led TVK government of allowing Tamil Nadu to become a hub for drug trafficking, likening the state to ‘Vice City’, a fictional world in the Grand Theft Auto (GTA) series.
Some time later, the Tamil Nadu Police posted two Grand Theft Auto (GTA)-themed posters showing its anti-narcotics operations in the state.
Vice City is a fictional, crime-ridden city inspired by 1980s Miami, where players engage in gang wars, drug trafficking, robberies and other criminal activities.

“With the continued deterioration of law and order, alleged sexual misconduct by TVK members, major robberies and horrifying custodial deaths, Tamil Nadu is turning into a Vice City under TVK rule,” Stalin said on Thursday.
The remarks came after the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) seized 70 kg of heroin worth ₹140 crore from a vehicle during a check in Chennai's Madhavaram on Thursday.

items.title: India’s six listed REITs distribute ₹3,234 crore in Q2
points: India’s six listed Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs) collectively distributed over ₹3,234 crore to more than 5.25 lakh unitholders in the second quarter of FY27, according to the Indian REITs Association.

The six REITs — Brookfield India Real Estate Trust, Embassy Office Parks REIT, Mindspace Business Parks REIT, Nexus Select Trust, Knowledge Realty Trust, and Bagmane Prime Office REIT — manage over 215 million square feet of Grade A office and retail space…

items.title: Marinakis-backed Capital Tankers gets Oslo main board green light
points: Evangelos Marinakis-backed Capital Tankers has secured approval to move its shares to Oslo’s main stock market, eight months after making its Norwegian trading debut through a $500m equity placement.

Oslo Børs confirmed on Thursday that it had decided to admit the Greek-controlled tanker owner to trading on the regulated Euronext Oslo Børs market, clearing a key hurdle in its planned transfer from Euronext Growth Oslo.
The decision follows an application submitted by Capital Tankers a day earlier and marks the next step in a listing strategy outlined when the company entered the Norwegian market in March.
Capital Tankers raised approximately NOK4.8bn ($500m), including the over-allotment arrangement, through its original placement, drawing strong institutional interest in its crude tanker portfolio.
The owner controls a fleet of 33 vessels, comprising 15 VLCCs, 10 suezmaxes and eight aframax/LR2 tankers.
Its latest fleet update showed 17 ships operating, with another 16 under construction for delivery through 2028.

items.title: Edit Instagram Stories After Posting: New Feature Gives Users a 15-Minute Window
points: Users will be able to make changes to their Stories for up to 15 minutes after sharing them.
Instagram launched Stories in 2016, letting users post photos and videos that disappear after 24 hours.
Now, a decade after its debut, the Meta-owned platform has announced a new feature that allows users to edit their Stories without losing engagement.
This long-awaited update gives users up to 15 minutes to make changes to the shared Stories.
Instagram head Adam Mosseri announced in a social media post on Wednesday that users can now edit Stories for up to 15 minutes after posting.
Instagram says modified Stories will have an 'Edited' label, allowing viewers to identify posts that have been changed after publication.
Users can access the editing option by opening the Story and selecting the three-dot menu at the bottom-right corner, then selecting Edit Story to make the required changes.

items.title: Sanctioned Tankers Carry 60% of Russian Oil in October: Monthly Intelligence Report
points: Sanctioned Tankers Carry 60% of Russian Oil in October Sixty percent of Russian oil was shipped on sanctioned tankers throughout October, supported by a rising number of new shadow fleet entrants over 2026 that are being used to offset freight logistics…

Analysis of tankers calling at Russian ports to load crude, fuel oil and refined products last month found that EU-owned tankers shipped 14% of volumes, one of the lowest percentages recorded this year.
Unsanctioned shadow fleet tankers accounted for 21% of all oil shipments, according to Windward analysis using data from Vortexa.
Sanctioned tankers were mostly used for crude shipments (69% of barrels shipped), followed by refined products (42%) and fuel oil (30%).
The overall figure of 60% carried on sanctioned tankers compares with 55% in September and 67% in March.

Naval Boardings Push Sanctioned Tankers To Reflag to Russian Of the 143 sanctioned tankers tracked calling at Russian Baltic, Black Sea, Arctic and Far East ports in October, 48% (69 ships) were flagged with Russia.

items.title: US ethanol offers lower GHG abatement costs than methanol, ammonia: study
points: Ethanol could abate about 2.09 metric tons of CO2 equivalent for every $1,000 spent on fuel, compared with 1.30 mt for low-carbon methanol and 1.73 mt for low-carbon ammonia, the Maritime Ethanol & Methanol Alliance, an initiative by the nonprofit Global…
MEMA estimated ethanol’s well-to-wake greenhouse gas intensity at 34.9 grams of CO2e/megajoule, compared with 15 gCO2e/MJ for low-carbon methanol and 10 gCO2e/MJ for low-carbon ammonia.

In the study, based on classification society ABS’s technical analysis, MEMA assumed US corn ethanol prices on a free-on-board Houston basis at $750/mt, equivalent to $1,125/mt of very low sulfur fuel oil on an energy-adjusted basis.
That compared with $1,200/mt, or $2,424/mt on a VLSFO-equivalent basis, for low-carbon methanol and $900/mt, or $1,945/mt VLSFOe, for low-carbon ammonia.
Delivered low-carbon methanol bunker prices in the Houston Ship Channel were $1,146.57/mt on the same day, according to Platts.

items.title: COSCO port fuels growth in APEC trade
points: Chancay Port in Peru, a vital APEC economy, has rapidly evolved into a pivotal logistics hub connecting Latin America with Asia, breathing life into the vision of a seamlessly interconnected Asia-Pacific.
Inaugurated in November 2024, the port was hailed by Chinese President Xi Jinping as the starting point of an Inca Trail of the New Era.

By slashing the one-way maritime transit time between Peru and China from roughly 35 days to just 23 days, the deep-water port has reduced logistics costs by more than 20 percent, fundamentally reshaping trans-Pacific trade dynamics.
The $3.5 billion smart port has not only revolutionized Peru’s foreign trade, but also catalyzed economic integration across the broader Latin American region.

With the launch of new feeder services like the Chancay Express Service 3 — known as CHX3 — which links Peru with Costa Rica, Chancay’s reach now extends to neighboring countries such as Brazil, Ecuador, Colombia and Chile.

items.title: Iraq resumes oil exports through Turkish pipeline after 12-year break
points: After a 12-year hiatus, Iraq has resumed pumping oil through a Turkish pipeline at an initial capacity of 120,000 barrels per day, as the conflict between the US and Iran continues to disrupt oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz.
The Iraqi Ministry of Oil said on Tuesday that it planned gradually to increase export capacity to 500,000 barrels a day.
Oil Minister Basim Mohammed Khudair said the reopening of the 960-kilometer Kirkuk-Ceyhan pipeline followed maintenance and rehabilitation work, and technical and operational testing.
It was forced offline by Daesh attacks in 2014.
He added that exports through this northern route allowed Iraq to sell crude oil at market prices without discounts, the Iraqi News Agency reported.
Iraq’s southern oil terminals have been affected by the Iran war, which began in late February, as Tehran has effectively blocked tankers from using the Strait of Hormuz.
Iraq is the second-largest producer in the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries, after Saudi Arabia.

items.title: Coal is back: Which German power plants are the biggest winners from the energy crisis?

items.title: Soybeans Fall as Dollar Firms
points: Soybean futures fell around $12.1 per bushel, easing from multi-week highs as a surging US dollar weighed on the broader grain complex.

The greenback climbed to a 19-month high on growing expectations of an interest-rate hike next month, making US supplies more expensive for overseas buyers and reducing their appeal against competing origins.
Higher-than-expected US soybean oil stocks also weighed on the vegetable oil market, while lower energy prices further weakened soybean oil and contributed to declines across other commodities.
Meanwhile, grain markets continued to monitor the outcome of the Trump-Xi meeting, with Chinese purchases of US agricultural products remaining a key point in bilateral trade discussions.

China is nearing its separate commitment to buy 25 million tonnes of US soybeans this year, but progress on a broader $17 billion farm-purchase pledge has lagged, leaving uncertainty over the outlook for US export demand.
